Above the ground the shape is free: roofs, towers, chimneys and machinery may differ from the block and may overhang a little. The dark openings in the block-out show where the front door, or a depot's train portals, are; keep them in those walls.

Do not paint the plinth itself: no ground, floor slab, pavement, grass or shadow under or around the building. A real RGBA PNG with a transparent background (alpha zero) and opaque building surfaces.

Never: rails, trains, people, vehicles, smoke, lettering, signs with text, borders, glow, or loose objects standing apart from the building.

Age: Steam. Steam age, the first railway: small and rural. Timber framing, cream limestone, warm brick, slate roofs, cast-iron posts, evergreen-painted woodwork, a chimney where it makes sense.

The palette family of the whole game: forest green #294638, moss #78804C, oat cream #E4D5B5, limestone #BCA98B, slate #626B6C, teal #477B82, copper #A36B42. Light from the upper left: roofs and tops lightest, lower-left walls mid, lower-right walls darkest.

Camera: keep the block-out's camera exactly. Orthographic 2:1 isometric, ground edges two pixels across for each pixel down, vertical edges vertical, no perspective. Do not rotate or tilt the view. Do not turn the building towards the viewer: the lower-right wall is seen as much from the side as the lower-left wall. Show the whole building with a clear margin all round: nothing touches the edge of the picture.

Footprint: the grey plinth is the building's footprint. The building stands on it and fills it: its outer walls rise from the plinth's edges, and at ground level nothing reaches outside the plinth. Keep the foot of the two visible walls plain and straight from corner to corner, so that it shows where the building stands: no bushes, crates, steps or loose objects in front of it. Above the ground the shape is free: roofs, towers, chimneys and machinery may differ from the block and may overhang a little. The dark openings in the block-out show where the front door, or a depot's train portals, are; keep them in those walls.

Do not paint the plinth itself: no ground, floor slab, pavement, grass or shadow under or around the building. A real RGBA PNG with a transparent background (alpha zero) and opaque building surfaces.

Never: rails, trains, people, vehicles, smoke, lettering, signs with text, borders, glow, or loose objects standing apart from the building.

Age: Steam. Steam age, the first railway: small and rural. Timber framing, cream limestone, warm brick, slate roofs, cast-iron posts, evergreen-painted woodwork, a chimney where it makes sense.
